title: a person who ... a thing that/which ... (relative clauses 1)
subtitle: a woman who can speak six languages
summary: Join two sentences into one with who for people and that or which for things.

lesson.heading: she -> who
lesson.text: At a restaurant a woman tells you: 'I can speak six languages.' Later you talk about her. You can say two sentences: *I met a woman. **She** can speak six languages.* Or you can make one sentence: **she** becomes **who**.

examples.text: I met a woman. **She** can speak six languages.
I met **a woman who** can speak six languages.

lesson.heading: it -> that or which
lesson.text: Jack is wearing a very big hat. It comes down over his eyes. We say: *Jack was wearing a hat. **It** was too big for him.* In one sentence, **it** becomes **that** or **which**.

examples.text: Jack was wearing **a hat that** was too big for him.
Jack was wearing **a hat which** was too big for him.

lesson.heading: who, that or which?
rows: A thief is a person **who** steals things.
An aeroplane is a machine **that** flies.
Emma lives in a house **which** is 400 years old.

lesson.heading: who is for people
lesson.text: Use **who** after a person, a friend, the man, the people, somebody, anybody, everybody. Do not use **who** for things.

examples.text: A thief is a person **who** steals things.
Do you know anybody **who** can play the piano?
The man **who** phoned didn't give his name.
The people **who** work in the office are very friendly.

lesson.heading: that is for things or people
lesson.text: **that** is possible for things and for people. For people, **who** is more usual.

examples.text: An aeroplane is a machine **that** flies.
Emma lives in a house **that** is 400 years old.
The people **that** work in the office are very friendly.

lesson.heading: which is for things
lesson.text: **which** is for things only. Never use **which** for people.

examples.text: An aeroplane is a machine **which** flies.
Emma lives in a house **which** is 400 years old.
Do you remember the woman **who** was playing the piano at the party?

lesson.text: People take who or that. Things take which or that. Never say ~~a machine who~~ or ~~a person which~~.

exercises.prompt: A thief is a person ___ steals things.
exercises.explanation: A person is a people word, so we use who (or that).

exercises.prompt: An aeroplane is a machine ___ flies.
exercises.explanation: A machine is a thing, so we use which or that - never who.

exercises.prompt: Match each person with what they do: A ... is a person who ... .

exercises.statement: I know somebody who works in that shop.
exercises.explanation: Correct. somebody is a person, so who is right.

exercises.prompt: What's the name of the river ___ flows through the town?
exercises.explanation: A river is a thing, so we use which (or that).

exercises.statement: A coffee maker is a machine who makes coffee.
exercises.explanation: A coffee maker is a machine that makes coffee. We do not use who for things.

exercises.prompt: A man phoned. He didn't give his name. Make one sentence.
exercises.answer: The man who phoned didn't give his name.
exercises.explanation: he becomes who, and who goes straight after the man.

exercises.prompt: A woman opened the door. She was wearing a yellow dress. The woman ___ the door was wearing a yellow dress.
exercises.explanation: she becomes who, and the verb stays in the past: who opened.

exercises.prompt: Does each sentence need who or which?

items.text: the man ... has just started work in your office
the river ... flows through the town
anybody ... wants to buy a car
a friend ... is very good at repairing cars
clothes ... are too small for him

exercises.statement: My neighbour bought a car who cost £40,000.
exercises.explanation: My neighbour bought a car that cost £40,000. A car is a thing, so we use that or which.

exercises.prompt: Some students took the exam. Most of them passed. Most of the students ___ the exam passed.
exercises.explanation: The students are people, so we use who, and the verb is past: who took.

exercises.prompt: A policeman stopped our car. He wasn't very friendly. Make one sentence.
exercises.answer: The policeman who stopped our car wasn't very friendly.
exercises.explanation: he becomes who, and the who-part comes straight after the policeman.
